newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 15.

text.p: Parliament dumps bill on shop trading: Parliament on Wednesday night voted 82-23 to stop legislation that would have abolished all shop trading hour regulations, despite appeals for it to be sent to a select committee so that the public could make submissions. Page 2.

National MP joins apponents of plan: National MP John Carter, the Government chief whip, joined the chorus of opposition to the compulsory superannuation proposal on Wednesday, saying it was inequitable and would deny people the right to choose their own method of saving. Page 2.
Parliament throws out Moore's bill to crack down on gangs: Parliament threw out a private member's bill introduced by Labour MP Mike Moore to crack down on gangs on Wednesday. Page 2.

Blow aimed at Shipley's leadership prospects: NZ First and senior Beehive sources aimed a blow at State Services Minister Jenny Shipley's National leadership prospects on Wednesday by suggesting the coalition deal could be off if she replaced Prime Minister Jim Bolger. Page 2.

Maori claim disappoints ministers: The government said on Wednesday it was disappointed that Maori groups had gone to the Waitangi Tribunal over Maori broadcasting policy, and urged them not to deflect the issue with another legal process. Page 2.

McDonald's paid $15m for rival outlets: McDonald's restaurant chain paid Progressive Enterprises $15 million for 17 Georgie Pie restaurants, the latest Overseas Investment Commission report says. Page 17.
WestpacTrust starts off well: New Zealand's biggest bank, WestpacTrust, announced a profit on Wednesday of $204 million for the half-year to the end of March 1997. Page 18.
Paynter losses continue: Paynter Timber Group has announced a higher annual bottom-line loss and is not predicting a return to profit until the second half of the current fiancial year. Page 25.

Exchange says Apple Fields report 'jumped the gun': The Stock Exchange says a report Apple Fields for not providing enough information on its proposed change from orchardist to property developer had "jumped the gun". Page 25.
IRD seeks winebox taxes from CHH: The Inland Revenue Department has made two assessments against Carter Holt Harvey over winebox deals using its "anti-avoidance" provisions. Page 25.
Price spat shuts magazine: Staff at one of New Zealand's two main computer magazines were delivered a bombshell this week: their magazine has been abruptly closed.
Brierley up on Weeks 'sale': Brierley Investments is understood to be close to selling its Australian oil asset Weeks Bass Strait Royalty for about $350 million.
Maori International to wind up after 13 years in tourism: A major Maori business venture established 13 years ago by former Maori Affairs secretary Kara Puketapu is being wound up.
